attack_surfaces.reason: Counter uses modulo 288 (magic 0xe38e38e38e38e38f, shr 8, multiply by 288) but reply pointer array only has 36 entries (0x120 bytes). When counter reaches 36-287, index goes OOB into stack: idx 36 hits rbp-0x110 (read buffer), idx 69 hits rbp-0x8 (canary), idx 70 hits rbp (saved rbp), idx 71 hits rbp+0x8 (return address). User controls the bytes at rbp-0x110 via read, so user-controlled data is dereferenced as a pointer by printf. Verified: GDB shows crash in printf with rdi=0x4141410a41414141 (user input bytes treated as pointer).

printf(array[counter]) where array[counter] for counter>=36 reads 8 bytes from user-controlled read buffer and dereferences them as a string pointer. If attacker places a valid pointer in the first 8 bytes of input, printf will use the pointed-to string as format string, enabling format string attacks (%s for arb read, %n for arb write) if the pointed-to memory contains format specifiers.

The modulo-288 computation allows indices 36-287 to read 8-byte values from stack addresses rbp-0x110 through rbp+0x6C8. This reads past the 36-entry array into: read buffer (idx 36-67), canary (idx 69), saved rbp (idx 70), return address (idx 71), and further up the stack. Any 8-byte value read this way is passed to printf as a format string pointer.
